definitions.explanation: Describes doing something because there is no other option, even though one would prefer not to. Emphasizes that the action is taken out of necessity rather than desire.

examples.japanese: やむなく{中止|ちゅうし}した。
examples.english: We had no choice but to cancel.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まり、やむなくタクシーで{帰|かえ}った。
examples.english: The trains stopped, so I reluctantly took a taxi home.

examples.japanese: {予算|よさん}の{都合|つごう}で、やむなく{計画|けいかく}を{縮小|しゅくしょう}することになった。
examples.english: Due to budget constraints, we had no choice but to scale back the plan.

notes:
An adverbial form derived from {止|や}むなし (unavoidable), itself from the verb {止|や}む (to cease, to stop). Conveys that the speaker or subject acts only because circumstances leave no alternative.

USAGE:
Used in both spoken and written Japanese, though it has a slightly formal or stiff quality. Common in news reports, business communication, and narrative writing. In casual speech, しかたなく or しょうがなく are more natural.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- やむなく{中止|ちゅうし}する — to cancel unavoidably
- やむなく{断念|だんねん}する — to reluctantly give up
- やむなく{辞退|じたい}する — to withdraw reluctantly
- やむなく{同意|どうい}する — to agree reluctantly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- しかたなく — reluctantly; more casual and conversational
- しょうがなく — reluctantly; casual, often implies mild resignation
- やむを{得|え}ず — unavoidably; more formal written variant with the same meaning
